chapter: Repertory band and wrap-up of day two
title: Harvey Estrin and the Sauter-Finegan rehearsal band
summary: The library moved from Price's barn to Potsdam and the YMHA.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: How did that whole business of Harvey Estran and the live studio orchestra and everything originate? How long has that been going?
About four or five years now.
When we gave up the band our library was parked in George Price's barn in Tenafly, New Jersey.
How did so much music end up in barns?
Because there was usually a lot of it and it's out of the way.

Ray Shriner, the oboist, was teaching at Pottsdam and had been with the college orchestra out there; he had some of the things. I don't know how he got it but he had it and he wanted the rest of it and he was coming down to get the stuff out of George Price's barn. So he came down one day and carted it up to Pottsdam. Six months later (inaudible) Harvey at the Y--
Harvey had the choice of getting the normal Nestico and Neal Hefti stocks and running the thing and thought,
point. I'm sure that has to hurt Harvey, I'm sure he's got certain ambitions but he guards the stuff, I have to give him credit for that. He doesn't let it out of his sight.
Yes (inaudible) And the other thing that bothers me--
You were saying something bothers you.

It's over amplified in the hall--they play in the hall at the Y that really needs a minimum of amplification. It doesn't have to do that, that band would sound great with none, in that room.
